terms.meaning: A web address the app answers, such as one that returns the demo data.
A fixed, previously recorded run that the demo always replays.
A structured picture of one run, grouped into rings, tiles and slides.
The route reads data and never changes it.

sections.name: File setup, TOOLS, registerCollationRoutes
sections.title: Imports and the list of tools
sections.what: Brings in the database tables, the login check and the collation helpers. Lists the two tools whose runs can be read by the single-run route: reality-scan and lessons-learnt.
sections.why: The header comment lists the three read-only views this file provides for the dark-mode demo.
sections.watch_out: Only the two names in the tool list are accepted by the single-run route, so a new tool must be added there or it is rejected.

sections.name: get
sections.title: Recorded datapoints for the code brain
sections.what: Returns the real Yard datapoints built by brainFragments to logged-in users. On failure it returns a 500 with a generic message.
sections.why: The header comment says this feeds the code brain view with real datapoints.
sections.watch_out: The real cause of a failure is only written to the server log, so the user sees a generic message.

sections.name: get
sections.title: Lists the pinned demo runs
sections.what: Reports which two recorded runs the dark demo replays, one reality scan and one lessons learnt run, with the time each was recorded. An entry is empty when its run is not in succeeded status.
sections.why: Likely reason: the demo should only show runs known to have completed well. The succeeded check is in the code, but the full reason is not stated.
sections.watch_out: A pinned run that is not succeeded gives an empty entry with no error, which can look like a missing run.

sections.name: get
sections.title: Picture of one run
sections.what: Given a tool name and a run ID, returns the collation model for that run. Returns 400 for an unknown tool and 404 if the run does not exist.
sections.why: The header comment says this is the read-only model of one run, shown as rings, tiles and slides.
sections.watch_out: The tool name must appear in the tool list at the top of this file, otherwise the reply is BAD_TOOL even when the run exists.

summary: Three read-only web routes that feed the dark-mode demo: recorded data points, the pinned demo runs, and the picture of one run.
purpose: Lets the dark-mode demo show real recorded runs without changing any data.
why: The header comment says these are read-only views over recorded data.
how: Each route first requires a logged-in user. It then reads from the database or from a helper module and returns JSON. Errors are logged on the server and the user gets a generic 500 reply. The single-run route checks the tool name before it looks anything up.
inputs: A logged-in request. For the single-run route, a tool name and a run ID in the web address. Database rows for pinned runs. The brainFragments helper output.
outputs: JSON: the recorded datapoints; the label and recorded time of each pinned run, or null if the run is not succeeded; a model of one run; or an error JSON with a code such as BAD_TOOL or NOT_FOUND.
risks: A pinned run that is not in succeeded status is hidden without any error, so the demo can look empty. Data is read from the database on every request, and no cache is visible in this file.
debug: If the demo shows nothing, check that the pinned run IDs exist and have succeeded status. A BAD_TOOL reply means the tool name is wrong. A NOT_FOUND reply means the run ID is not in the database. For 500 errors, look at server log lines starting with collation.
